title: add-jsonschema-v2-response-format-with-strict-streaming-fallback
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a new response_format 'json_schema_v2' with streaming-aware partial validation and explicit schema violation errors. Backwards compatible by default; opt-in strict streaming mode available. SDK patches and docs included.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers using structured output and the OpenAI-compat layer continue to hit edge cases when models stream tokens that transiently violate the declared JSON schema (for example: truncated objects mid-stream or tokens that later get corrected). This PR implements a new response_format value json_schema_v2 that performs lightweight, streaming-aware partial validation during token emission, surfaces structured schema_violation events to clients, and provides a strict_mode toggle that upgrades behavior to immediate request rejection on strong violations.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a streaming-safe JSON Schema v2 validator to the runtime, maps OpenAI-compat response_format json_schema_v2 to the new validator, updates SDKs to surface structured error events, and introduces a fallback path where strict_mode=false will gracefully fall back to best-effort streaming with a final post-stream validation result.

Detailed behavior: - response_format=json_schema_v2 (default strict_mode=false): runtime performs incremental token-level validation and emits progress events of type 'schema_hint' and final 'schema_result'. If final validation fails, the response contains an explicit structured error block and a new error code SVC-1003. The streaming connection itself remains open unless strict_mode=true. - response_format=json_schema_v2 & strict_mode=true: runtime attempts incremental validation and will abort the stream and return an immediate structured error when a non-recoverable violation is detected (e.g. unmatched braces in a way that cannot be reconciled by later tokens, or missing required top-level keys when end-of-stream is reached). - Backwards compatibility: response_format=json_schema (legacy) behavior unchanged. Clients that do not opt into json_schema_v2 continue to get current behavior.

OpenAI-compat specifics: The compatibility shim accepts the parameter response_format=json_schema_v2 (same semantics), and maps incoming strict=true to strict_mode=true in Redwood API. We explicitly document that OpenAI-style field names 'response_format' and 'strict' are translated. This allows smooth migration for customers currently using the OpenAI-compat endpoint.

Runtime changes (high-level): - Added runtime/validation/jsonschema_v2.py: incremental validator with token buffer heuristics and a light-weight recovery model to avoid false positives mid-stream. - Serving runtime hooks: emit structured stream control events (schema_hint, schema_violation, schema_result). - Fallback policy: when strict_mode=false, the runtime will continue streaming but annotate the response with final schema_result metadata and include a structured error if validation fails.

SDK and API surface updates: - Python and TypeScript SDKs: new response event types and helpers to subscribe to schema_hint/result events. - openai_compat layer: accepts response_format=json_schema_v2 and strict=true/false mapping. - Console/docs: new page documenting migration path and examples.

Testing and rollout: - Added unit tests and e2e streaming tests that simulate incremental partial outputs and model fluctuations (tests/e2e/test_stream_schema.py). - Canary rollout plan: feature flagged; start at 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours, monitor schema_violation metric and client error rates, then 50% for 24 hours, then 100% if metrics are green.

Migration notes for customers: Clients that want strict enforcement should pass strict_mode=true (or strict=true on OpenAI-compat). If you rely on legacy lenient behavior, do nothing. SDKs will include helpers to parse the structured error block and to receive schema_hint events to progressively build the validated payload.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime validator implementation - [x] OpenAI-compat mapping - [x] SDK surface updates (Python + TS) - [x] Docs and examples - [x] Unit and e2e tests - [x] Feature flag and rollout configuration

Related work: ENG-2476 (validation infra), PM-632 (product requirements for strict structured output).

CI and merge notes: initial CI run failed on a flaky test in tests/infra/test_rate_limiter; reran and all checks passed. This PR is merged by squash to keep history focused.
